problem: Existing VLN agents fail to connect semantic reasoning with spatial execution: intermediate (text/latent) reasoning is not anchored to image regions, and high-level decisions lack precise spatial goals for low-level motion. Direct-action VLMs need huge data, waypoint methods are bounded by candidate quality, and CoT methods stay ungrounded.
motivation: Cognitive science suggests human navigation is hierarchical: relevant landmarks are selectively encoded and gaze is directed to upcoming landing targets before stepping. Modern VLMs already have strong reasoning and pointing ability, so visual grounding can serve as a shared interface between cognition (VLM) and locomotion (geometric planner), improving accuracy and sample efficiency.
key_idea: Use visual grounding (coordinate-tagged landmarks in structured CoT plus a progress-aligned pixel goal) as the shared interface between VLM reasoning and a geometric low-level planner, trained with grounded CoT SFT data and execution-aware GRPO.
insight: Execution-aware RL (GEAR) contributes the most: removing it drops R2R-CE SR from 69.9 to 57.2, and replacing the reward map with 2D pixel distance drops it to 66.2. Grounded tags matter (-3.8 SR without <obj>/<prev_obj>), and temporal alignment of grounded evidence is important (62.2 SR without it). Correct grounding is associated with nearly double the action accuracy, and GEAR improves grounding recall/F1 and goal precision.
method: Structured reasoning with grounding: instruction decomposed once into ordered subtasks; each step does History Recall, Current Perception, Progress Estimation, Future Planning, with <obj>/<prev_obj> label|[x,y]</obj> tags in normalized [0,1000] coordinates binding evidence to the image.

Progress-aligned pixel-goal decision: VLM outputs MOVE/TURN/STOP; MOVE carries a subtask, label and pixel goal chosen as the furthest visible, traversable point within the current subtask segment (not the farthest visible point as in DualVLN); TURN is 90/180 degrees in place.

Low-level planner: RTAB-Map pose from RGB-D, point-cloud traversability map, back-projects pixel goal to 3D, A* path plus a path follower producing primitive actions; VLM invoked only at sparse decision steps (about 33% of steps).

GroundingCOTVLN-188K data engine: replay 21K R2R/RxR reference trajectories in Habitat with the planner, sample arrival/turn/mid-distance anchors, subtask-goal alignment, teacher VLM (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B) CoT synthesis, SAM 3 tracking with 3D world markers for temporal identity (<prev_obj>), and multi-check filtering.
SFT: one epoch on 188K samples with token-weighted CE plus a differentiable coordinate (expected-digit, SmoothL1) loss.

GEAR: GRPO (G=8, 16K anchors, 2000 steps) with an execution-aware pixel-goal reward map Q_t (route consistency, progress, execution-endpoint error, with traversability gating) plus action, subtask, and SAM3-verified grounding rewards and reasoning-consistency penalties.

setting.backbone: Qwen3.5-4B (SFT + GRPO fine-tuned) high-level VLM; RTAB-Map + A* low-level planner
setting.training_data: GroundingCOTVLN-188K (188K grounded image-CoT samples from 21K R2R and RxR trajectories, annotated by Qwen3.5-397B-A17B with SAM 3); GEAR on a 16K subset
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB-D (stitched left-front-right views), with pose estimated online by RTAB-Map; VLM uses RGB only
setting.action_space: High-level MOVE(pixel goal)/TURN/STOP converted by a geometric planner into primitive low-level turns and forward steps
setting.privileged: none at test time (sensor depth is required; the data engine uses GT reference paths only for training)

numbers_note: The real-world results are only given in a figure (success rates over 10 episodes per difficulty level); the ablation table numbers are on R2R-CE val-unseen (w/o GEAR: SR 57.2, SPL 49.5).
results: GroundingVLN reaches 69.9 SR / 64.1 SPL on R2R-CE and 75.1 SR / 62.0 SPL on RxR-CE val-unseen, beating ABot-N0 (66.4 / 69.3 SR) by 3.5 and 5.8 points, using 188K samples (about 0.9% of ABot-N0's data). In R2R-to-RxR transfer it gets 59.9 SR versus 39.8 for AwareVLN.
limitations: Low-level execution needs sensor metric depth and RGB-D SLAM; performance drops (SR 69.9 to 65.5) with noisy D435-like depth, which limits deployment on platforms without reliable depth.
Relies on a large teacher VLM (Qwen3.5-397B) and SAM 3 for data annotation and grounding rewards; teacher grounding annotations can contain errors.
General multimodal capability is only partly retained (MMStar 63.67 to 57.20, MVBench 50.93 to 45.55); real-world evaluation is small (10 episodes per level).
